target_customer: Professionals who want to meet new contacts in person, starting in early tech hubs
problem: Professional networking on LinkedIn is passive and does not produce real meetings; Weave aimed to turn connections into face to face introductions.
business_model: Consumer app, free to users; monetization not found

founders.name: Brian Ma
founders.background_notes: Background from TechCrunch 2014-05-01 and the YC page; YC page lists him as the only founder.

founders.name: Elpizo Choi
founders.background_notes: VentureBeat 2014-07-25 names him co-founder who helped build the mobile version of the CoffeeMe idea with Ma; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: The company told customers the service was not financially viable.

competitors.name: Treatings
competitors.what: Web service to filter and meet professionals, for example for informational interviews
competitors.traction_then: Web only with a mobile app planned; partnered with NYU's alumni network

competitors.name: CoffeeMe
competitors.what: Invite curated web network for meeting professionals over coffee in San Francisco and Seattle
competitors.traction_then: Web only, members vetted; shares an origin with Weave

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile apps, LinkedIn data import and a matching model using connection history were standard but nontrivial; the later AI matchmaking and scheduling added operational complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on local user density, which helps if reached, but LinkedIn controlled the data source and the swipe idea was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: LinkedIn stayed the data source and dominant network; no source shows it copying Weave. Weave shut down in July 2016.

market_need_then: Tinder style swiping was a hot pattern in 2014 and TechCrunch (2014-05-01) framed Weave as Tinder for professional networking; the company reported over 1,000 matches a week by mid 2014 according to coverage seen in search results.

branding.domain_note: Used weave.in rather than weave.com, per the YC page; the domain no longer resolves from this environment.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly sign off on YC page: Happy Weaving, with #startweaving hashtag and @startweaving Twitter handle.

branding.brand_signature: The #startweaving hashtag and the Tinder for professionals framing
branding.community_and_virality: Press framed it as Tinder for LinkedIn (VentureBeat, TechCrunch, Engadget in 2014); a Uber API partnership blog existed in 2015; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Short friendly real word but a very common one, and the press hook was borrowed from Tinder rather than from the brand itself.

pivots.from: Swipe based Tinder for LinkedIn networking app
pivots.to: AI based matchmaking with a curated weekly introduction, users no longer swipe or chat and Weave schedules the meeting
pivots.why: Described in VentureBeat 2016-01-19; the reason was not stated, and the date is that of the article.

outcome_analysis: Weave raised a 630 thousand dollar seed led by Vulcan Capital in July 2014 and, by press accounts, more than 2 million dollars in total with YC, Index Ventures, Vulcan and Eastlink. It moved from swipe based matching to a weekly AI introduction in early 2016, then told users in July 2016 that it was not financially viable. The company's own statement gives viability as the cause; no deeper post-mortem was found, so the pivot that failed to produce a viable business is the only factor assigned.
notes: Total raised: VentureBeat 2016 says more than 2 million dollars and names YC, Index Ventures, Vulcan Capital and Eastlink Ventures; CB Insights lists about 650K over four rounds with the last in 2016 (seen in a search summary only). Only the 630K seed is documented, so a gap of roughly 1.4 million dollars is unexplained and a search for a later round found only other companies named Weave. Shutdown date is the article date 2016-07-12 with the effective date likely 2016-07-18. PitchBook tags a merger or acquisition entry with no details; not confirmed. Company site did not resolve. Education not found.
